# suest for R

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/tdmize/suest/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tdmize/suest/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

`suest` lets you compare predictions and marginal effects across
regression models in R. It combines two or more separately fitted models
into one object with a joint robust covariance matrix. That object works
directly with [`marginaleffects`](https://marginaleffects.com/), so you
can calculate predictions and effects for each model and test whether
they differ across models.

Combining models this way is seemingly unrelated estimation, developed
by:

> Weesie, Jeroen. 1999. “Seemingly Unrelated Estimation and the
> Cluster-Adjusted Sandwich Estimator.” *Stata Technical Bulletin*
> 52:34–47.

The package implements the framework for comparing predictions and
marginal effects across models in:

> Mize, Trenton D., Long Doan, and J. Scott Long. 2019. “A General
> Framework for Comparing Predictions and Marginal Effects Across
> Models.” *Sociological Methodology* 49(1):152–189.
> [doi:10.1177/0081175019852763](https://doi.org/10.1177/0081175019852763)

The same framework is available in Stata through the [`mecompare`
command](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/mecompare).

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tdmize/suest")
```

## Basic usage

``` r

library(suest)
library(marginaleffects)

dat <- mtcars
dat$am <- factor(dat$am)

base <- glm(am ~ wt, family = binomial("logit"), data = dat)
adjusted <- glm(am ~ wt + hp, family = binomial("logit"), data = dat)
combined <- suest(base, adjusted, model_names = c("Base", "Adjusted"))

effects <- avg_comparisons(combined, variables = "wt", newdata = dat)
effects
hypotheses(effects, hypothesis = difference ~ revpairwise)
```

[`suest()`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md) accounts
for the covariance between estimates from different models. This is
essential when the models use the same or overlapping observations.

## Supported models

`suest` works with linear, binary, ordinal, multinomial, count,
censored, survival, and instrumental-variable models, as well as panel,
multilevel, and survey models. Models can use the same, partially
overlapping, or completely different samples. See the [full list of
supported
models](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/suest.html#supported-models).

- [Getting

  mediation](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/mediation.html),

  and [separate samples or
  groups](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/groups.html).
- More examples: [group
  comparisons](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/chapter-groups.html),
  [multilevel
  models](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/multilevel.html),

  graphs](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/predictions.html):
  predictions from each model, and tests and graphs of their

  tables](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/tables.html)
  of coefficients and marginal effects with `modelsummary`.
- [Notes on specific
  models](https://www.trentonmize.com/software/suest_r/articles/model-notes.html).

# Package index

## Core workflow

Combine models, pool imputed systems, and construct model-specific
evaluation data

- [`suest()`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md)
  [`coef(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md)
  [`nobs(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md)
  [`print(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest.md)
  : Combine fitted models with seemingly unrelated estimation
- [`suest_mi()`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  [`coef(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  [`nobs(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  [`summary(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  [`print(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_mi.md)
  : Pool SUEST systems across multiple imputations
- [`suest_newdata()`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_newdata.md)
  : Stack the estimation samples from a SUEST object
- [`suest_twopart()`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_twopart.md)
  [`print(`*`<suest_twopart>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/suest_twopart.md)
  : Two-part models

## Tables

Methods for modelsummary tables

- [`tidy(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/tidy.suest_model.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/tidy.suest_model.md)
  [`glance(`*`<suest_model>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/tidy.suest_model.md)
  [`glance(`*`<suest_mi>`*`)`](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/reference/tidy.suest_model.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for regression tables

# Articles

### Predictions and graphs

- [Predictions and
  graphs](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/predictions.md):

  Predictions from each model and their differences: Figures 3 to 6 of
  Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

### Regression tables

- [Regression
  tables](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/tables.md):

  Tables of coefficients and marginal effects across models with
  modelsummary.

### Examples: Mize, Doan & Long (2019)

- [Curvilinear effects and
  mediation/attenuation](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/mediation.md):

  Example 6.1 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

- [Nested logit models and
  mediation/attenuation](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/nested-models.md):

  Example 6.2 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

- [Alternative
  predictors](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/alternative-predictors.md):

  Example 6.3 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

- [Different
  outcomes](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/different-outcomes.md):

  Example 6.4 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

- [Different model
  types](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/model-types.md):

  Example 6.5 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019): ordinal versus nominal.

- [Separate samples or
  groups](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/groups.md):

  Example 6.6 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019).

### More examples

- [Group
  comparisons](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/chapter-groups.md):

  Section 4.2 of Mize and Han (forthcoming): separate models for each
  group.

- [Multilevel
  models](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/multilevel.md):

  Students nested in schools, and women nested in districts:
  mixed-effects logit and probit.

- [Panel models](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/panel.md):

  Repeated observations of the same people: random-effects logits and
  fixed-effects regressions for two outcomes.

- [Within-person
  effects](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/within-person.md):

  Correlated random effects (Mundlak) logits: the within-person effect
  compared with the random-effects estimate.

- [Instrumental-variable
  models](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/instrumental-variables.md):

  Comparing effects across two-stage least squares models with different
  instruments.

- [Two-part
  models](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/two-part.md):

  Effects on an outcome with many zeros, such as medical expenditures,
  from a two-part model.

### More

- [Notes on specific
  models](https://tdmize.github.io/suest/articles/model-notes.md):

  Settings and limits for a few of the supported models, and what to use
  for Stata models without an R version.
